prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: one full-bleed production illustration for a literary Bible passage. Requested canvas 1536x1024 pixels, landscape 3:2.
Primary request: Depict the oracle in Isaiah 11:1–9 as a prophetic vision of a righteous ruler and a peaceable creation. Show a green shoot growing from an old cut tree stump in the foreground, a dignified adult ruler in simple ancient Judean clothing standing nearby, and a small child safely among a clearly readable group of animals at rest. Include the text's wolf with lamb, leopard with young goat, calf and young lion, and bear and cow; do not turn it into a crowded animal collage. The child may lead the group along a quiet hillside.
Scene/backdrop: A restrained Levantine hillside with olive and terebinth foliage, dry-stone ground, and softly layered hills. The atmosphere is visionary and literary, not an observed historical landscape.
Style/medium: Realistic cinematic historical/literary illustration matching the supplied reference images' warm golden light, tactile earth, cloth, stone, and restrained realism. No fantasy costume or medieval aesthetic.
Composition/framing: Wide 3:2 landscape. Keep the stump and shoot, ruler, child, and animals entirely within the left 62% of the canvas. Group them legibly in one coherent scene. Leave the entire right 35–38% as low-detail soft hillside, pale sky, and distant foliage with quiet contrast suitable for reader text overlay. Keep the top and bottom 12% noncritical. No montage, collage, panels, or cutaway.
Lighting/mood: Warm late-afternoon gold, gentle, hopeful, contemplative; no dramatic battle or disaster.
Color palette: Ochre, muted olive, cream linen, sandstone, restrained gold, dusty green.
Materials/textures: Natural wool, woven linen, living green shoot, old bark, limestone, dry grasses, animal coats.
Interpretation: This is a prophetic vision. The peaceful proximity of predator and prey must read as visionary imagery, not an observed historical landscape, archaeological reconstruction, or fixed end-times interpretation. The ruler is a literary representation of the oracle; do not identify him with a named historical portrait. Show only visible visual cues; do not render the spirit of the LORD as a person, face, halo, beam, or humanlike being.
Avoid: Text, letters, captions, labels, verse numbers, pins, UI, logos, watermark, modern objects, buildings that imply a specific site, ornate religious iconography, deity or God-in-human-form, halos, glowing figures, graphic injury, predator aggression, empty landform diorama, tiny unreadable subject cluster, animal rows, or realistic interaction that makes the scene seem zoologically documented.
notes: Final raster reviewed against the named subjects; account-specific references remain in the scene registry. Historical appearances are reconstructed and literary scenes are labeled.
